Deep Bhattacharjee, *Two conjectures of Wormald on Hamilton cycles in tournaments*. Final revision, single column (amsart), 11 pages.

The paper proves Conjectures 2 and 6 of N. C. Wormald, *Tournaments with many Hamilton cycles*
(arXiv:2610.16245): for a regular tournament on d vertices with skew adjacency matrix S, his
Hessian determinant is H = d det(d^2 I + S^2)/det(d^2 I - S^2), so H is nonzero and d/H is the
square of a rational number, and for the cyclic tournaments sqrt(d/H) tends to
cosh 1 / cos 1 = 2.8559578925..., the constant he estimated. Every statement is proved by hand.
Programs in C, Python and PARI/GP check the identities on small cases; this release runs all of
them before publishing. No statement of the paper rests on them.

The results were first made public on 14 October 2026 as release v1.0.0 of
creelie/Breakthrough-problems-1; an earlier and incomplete version of the paper appeared on
Hexagon as hexagon:2610.00460.

Files: the paper (`WormaldHamiltonCycles_final2.pdf`), its LaTeX source with the figures
(`WormaldHamiltonCycles_final2-tex.zip`) and the arXiv tarball
(`WormaldHamiltonCycles_final2-arxiv.tar.gz`).
